title: Vendor Wallet & Receipt Handoff — conference scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for the vendor wallet handoff + receipt capture process for conference booths and on-site vendor purchases. Mix of notes to self, things to confirm, phone numbers, and a short checklist for handing the physical wallet back to ops after the event.

Top-level plan (high level):
- Vendor wallet = clear zip pouch with: 2x corporate cards (last4: 2379), petty cash $200 (USD), vendor receipts envelope, small receipt scanner/phone charging cable, printed purchase authorizations.
- Primary owner onsite: Elena Park (me) — if I'm on stage, handover to Miguel. Secondary: Priya Desai (back-up).

Pre-event (48–72h):
- Confirm vendor pick-up window with facilities (concourse B loading dock, bay 3). Note contact: Tony Liu, facilities lead, +1 (415) 555-0127, t.liu@vendorops.example.com.
- Photo of corporate cards front/back to secure drive? NO — security policy says no photos. Use card last4 in notes only.
- Load expense tool: pre-create receipt groups in ExpenseX under trip code EX-3421 (linked). Tag: REDWOOD-BOOTH-MAR25.
- Print 20 blank receipt envelopes (labelled by category: travel, meals, hardware, services).
- Bring 2x ziplock bags for wet receipts (drinks/coffee).

Onsite: vendors & logistics notes:
- Badge and vendor kit pick-up: exhibitor desk opens 07:30. Bring exhibitor confirmation email + ID.
- Vendor deliveries: schedule arrival slot 09:00–11:00 to avoid forklift congestion. Keep Tony's number handy.
- Recommended local vendor contacts (handy if we need last-minute cable/stand):
  * QuickStands SF — contact: Priya Nair, +1 (415) 555-0911, priya@quickstands.co, typical lead time 2–3h for small orders.
  * ChargeRunner rentals — contact: Omar Vaz, +1 (650) 555-2234, omar@chargerunner.io (power strips, fast chargers).
  * Booth Catering (on-call) — Paula Gomez, +1 (415) 555-0789 (small snack trays, receipts by email).
- If vendor takes card, insist on itemized receipt (no generic $XX). For cash purchases get a handwritten receipt with vendor name, date, amount, and itemization.

Expense capture process (best practice):
- Immediately photograph every receipt with the phone app (ExpenseX) — use the "Booth Receipts" folder. Tag with vendor name and expense category.
- For vendor invoices >$500: request emailed invoice, upload to ExpenseX, and mark for Accounts Payable (AP) review.
- Foreign currency: note the local amount and approximate USD conversion in the receipt notes; final conversion done by ExpenseX / bank statement reconciliation.
- Meal per-diem reminder: standard policy = $75/day per person for the event city (verify Confluence link before submitting).

Receipt handoff & wallet return (post-event):
- Wrap-up time: within 48 hours of booth strike, consolidate all receipts into labelled envelopes.
- Quick reconciliation: count cash left in wallet and take a photo of contents (safely) — amount should match petty cash log. Log (simple): date, starting cash $200, cash spent $XX, remaining $YY, initials (Elena).
- Handoff to Travel Ops: meet at SF office mailroom on Mon 10:00 or schedule drop-off with Miguel. If mailing, use FedEx pre-paid label (expense category: shipping).
- Fill out the ExpenseX trip summary: attach photos + envelopes scanned. Add notes for any missing receipts (explain why).

Common pitfalls / things to avoid:
- Do not let vendors keep corporate cards overnight. If vendor insists, escalate to facilities and travel-ops.
- Don’t accept receipts with handwritten ambiguous totals (e.g., line scratched out). Ask vendor to reprint or initial corrected total.
- Avoid taking pictures of cards or sensitive details — redact PAN except last4 before upload if accidentally captured.

Open questions / follow-ups for Travel Ops team:
- Confirm petty cash float amount (is $200 still supported or should we request $300 for West Coast events?). @Miguel — can you check petty cash policy?
- Who is authorized to sign vendor authorizations on behalf of Redwood at the show? Need official list for the front desk.
- Insurance/incident: if a vendor damages booth hardware, what's the immediate claims contact? Add to emergency card.

Quick checklist (tick boxes in head):
- [ ] Confirm exhibitor pick-up window + bring confirmation email
- [ ] Print labelled receipt envelopes (20)
- [ ] Charge corporate cards + save last4 in notes
- [ ] Add trip code EX-3421 in ExpenseX + pre-create groups
- [ ] Call QuickStands & ChargeRunner for standby numbers
- [ ] Pack petty cash + tape + sharpie + spare zip ties
- [ ] Final wallet handoff plan confirmed with Miguel (time/place)

Emergency contacts (on-call):
- Facilities: Tony Liu +1 (415) 555-0127
- Travel Ops: Miguel Alvarez +1 (415) 555-0899, miguel.alvarez@redwood.com
- Backup: Priya Desai +1 (415) 555-0456, priya.desai@redwood.com

Notes to self (short):
- If short on receipt detail, ask vendor for a stamped invoice (works best for small hardware).
- For Lyft/Uber shared rides: capture screenshot with route and fare breakdown if receipt is missing.
- Keep receipts in chronological order in the envelope to speed reconciliation.

End-of-doc: will convert into a small two-sided one-sheet for the booth lead with the top contacts + handoff checklist. For now, keep as scratchpad and iterate after the event.

Unresolved/To log after event:
- Final petty cash spent breakdown and scanned petty cash envelope image.
- Any vendor disputes (missing itemized receipts) — list vendor, amount, desired remedy.

---
Edited notes (2025-03-04): Miguel confirmed FedEx pre-paid labels available; petty cash is OK at $250 if requested 72h in advance. Updated contact: Paula (catering) now uses catering@boothcater.example.com for invoices.
